fact: 1944年7月1日至22日，来自44个国家的700余名代表在美国新罕布什尔州布雷顿森林的华盛顿山饭店召开联合国货币与金融会议，规划战后国际货币与金融秩序。

sources.title: 80 Years Since the Bretton Woods Conference | The Bretton Woods Committee
sources.quote: During 1-22 July 1944 over 700 representatives from 44 countries met in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire for the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference.

sources.title: IMF Timeline | International Monetary Fund
sources.quote: Representatives of 44 Allied nations, seeking to avoid the mistakes that led to Depression and World War II, meet to plan a new economic order built on global cooperation.

fact: 布雷顿森林会议发起设立国际货币基金组织（IMF）与国际复兴开发银行（IBRD，即世界银行前身），并建立以可调整固定汇率为核心的战后货币体系。

sources.title: 80 Years Since the Bretton Woods Conference | The Bretton Woods Committee
sources.quote: by launching the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD).

sources.title: IMF Timeline | International Monetary Fund
sources.quote: They set up a system of exchange rates linked to the U.S. dollar, while the IBRD was created to finance postwar reconstruction.

fact: 1944年6月22日，罗斯福签署《军人调整法》（Servicemen's Readjustment Act，即GI法案），向二战退伍军人提供大学教育资助（每学年最高约500美元学费与书费）、52周失业补助和政府担保低息房贷；到1951年近800万退伍军人使用了教育与培训福利。

sources.title: Servicemen's Readjustment Act (1944) | National Archives
sources.quote: Signed into law by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on June 22, 1944, this act, also known as the G.I. Bill, provided World War II veterans with funds for college education, unemployment insurance, and housing.

sources.title: S. 1767, G.I. Bill of Rights | U.S. Capitol Visitor Center
sources.quote: The act provided returning soldiers with 52 weeks of unemployment insurance; money for post-secondary education and job training; and government-backed, low-interest mortgages. By 1951 nearly 8 million veterans had received educational and training benefits.

fact: 美国实际国民生产总值从1939年的886亿美元增长到1944年的1350亿美元；战争相关生产在1943年已占GNP的40%（战前仅约2%）。1944年名义GDP约1748亿美元。

sources.title: The American Economy during World War II | EH.net
sources.quote: The gross national product of the U.S., as measured in constant dollars, grew from $88.6 billion in 1939 ... to $135 billion in 1944. War-related production skyrocketed from just two percent of GNP to 40 percent in 1943.

fact: 在1942年4月至1946年6月联邦最严格物价管制期间，美国年通胀率仅约3.5%，而管制前六个月年通胀率约为10.3%；战时工资与物价管制成功抑制了通胀。

sources.title: The American Economy during World War II | EH.net
sources.quote: Between April 1942 and June 1946, the period of the most stringent federal controls on inflation, the annual rate of inflation was only 3.5 percent; the annual rate had been 10.3 percent in the six months preceding April.

fact: 战时航空工业是美国战时经济最大部门：以1939年为100，美国飞机产量指数1944年达约2805；整个战时共生产超过12.5万架飞机，雇佣约200万工人，耗资约450亿美元。

sources.title: The American Economy during World War II | EH.net
sources.quote: American aircraft production was the single largest sector of the war economy, costing $45 billion ... employing a staggering two million workers, and ... producing over 125,000 aircraft.

fact: 战时全国工资理事会（NWLB）将战时工资涨幅限制在约15%（对应1941年1月至1942年5月生活成本涨幅），并对汽油、食糖、肉类等实行配给；普通人实际生活成本受管制但仍有隐性挤压。

sources.title: The American Economy during World War II | EH.net
sources.quote: In July, the National War Labor Board (NWLB) limited wartime wage increases to about 15 percent, the factor by which the cost of living rose from January 1941 to May 1942.

fact: 战时个人收入普遍增加，许多美国人预期战后物质生活会持续改善，但也有人担心战后重回大萧条；这种“复员后需求释放”与“衰退担忧”并存，构成1945年资产布局的心理背景。

sources.title: The American Economy during World War II | EH.net
sources.quote: the substantial increases in personal income and frequently, if not always, in quality of life during the war led many Americans to foresee permanent improvements to their material circumstances, even as others feared a postwar return of the depression.
